why: Seasonal-lease campground with no nightly sales and no web presence (read 2026-11-19): Gov. of Saskatchewan release 2015-10-20 (saskatchewan.ca .../2015/october/20/sask-landing-investment) calls the park's private campgrounds 'long-term, full-service, seasonal' with 'the ability to remain in the same site, year over year' and says the first such development 'opened 80 full-service campsites in 2010 and is fully occupied' - by elimination Landing View (the park's other private businesses are Cactus Blume, 2016, and Glamping Resorts' canvas cabins); a 2026-04-26 park review (acrockofschmidt.com) calls Landing View 'this seasonal campground' and 'I can't find any information about this seasonal campground online'; no operator website, booking page, Tourism Saskatchewan listing or Google Maps place found (Google returns only the provincial park for the name); Esri imagery at 50.6640,-107.9660 shows a dense treed RV grid of parked units west of Hwy 4 by the golf course. Fails long-stay test 2 (no nightly rate or booking site) and the private presence rule.
name: Landing View Private Campground
flags: Named 'Landing View Private Campground' on the Sask Parks core-area map (saskparks.tourismsaskatchewan.com .../saskatchewan-landing-all.pdf, p.1) at ~50.6640,-107.9660, west of Hwy 4 opposite the marina; not in campgrounds.json (nearest entries 9205 at 1.9 km, 15717 at 3.5 km, 15716 at 3.9 km).
Not waterfront in any case: Hwy 4, the marina lot and ~300 m+ of ground lie between the grid and Lake Diefenbaker.

Lead 5 (Cactus Blume) is the 2015 Cactus Blume Campground Ltd. development, which the same release describes as a 125-site seasonal campground; the 2026 review gives 166 seasonal sites and Tourism Saskatchewan calls it 'long-term seasonal' - likely the same skip.
